words.sense: Provoke intense anger or outrage in someone.
misconceptions: Any provocative message that angers people necessarily incites them.

words.sense: Stir or urge people to take action, often harmful or unlawful.
words.connotation: often strongly negative; linked to provocation
misconceptions: An instruction to act is merely an expression of anger.

semantic_axes.description: Outrage felt by recipients versus actions the message pushes them to take.
Presence of a call to do something rather than just an insult.

edges.boundary_rule: To incense people is to make them furious; to incite people is to spur them toward an action, not merely a feeling.
clues_a: recipients fume or demand an apology
clues_b: speaker tells a group what to do next
message urges people to break a rule
irrelevant_clues: whether people agree with the speaker

misconceptions.M1: Any provocative message that angers people necessarily incites them.
misconceptions.M2: An instruction to act is merely an expression of anger.
misconceptions.M3: The crowd’s size or noise alone determines the verb.

chains.frame: Which word best describes what Rina’s review did to diners?

beats.text: Rina’s review mocked customers who ordered the cheapest meals; readers flooded the comments with angry complaints.
beats.reason: The review provoked indignation among its readers.

beats.text: Several readers demanded that she apologize for insulting people on small budgets.
beats.decisive_clue: the response focuses on demanding an apology for the insult
beats.reason: The apology demands confirm outrage at the insult, not a push from Rina toward some action.

chains.feedback_short: The apology demands confirm outrage at the insult, not a push from Rina toward some action.
chains.feedback_deep: The review provoked indignation among its readers. The apology demands confirm outrage at the insult, not a push from Rina toward some action. Incense creates outrage; incite pushes people to act.
chains.contrast_rule: Incense creates outrage; incite pushes people to act.

hints.attention: Look at the effect on the readers.
hints.axis: Outrage felt by recipients versus actions the message pushes them to take.
hints.contrast: Incense creates outrage; incite pushes people to act.
